questions.question: In which of the following locations can you build large dams to generate hydel power?

__
 
• **Hilly terrains **are suitable for **building large dams** to **generate hydel power** as they have fast-flowing rivers and steep slopes, which create a significant amount of **potential energy.**
 
• The construction of** large dams** requires a significant amount of **water flow, **which is not available in **desert areas.**
 
• Therefore, building large dams in desert areas is **not feasible** for generating hydel power.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hydel power** is generated by using the** potential energy of falling water** to rotate turbines, which, in turn, generate electricity.
 
• **Large dams** are typically built in** hilly terrains**, where there is a **high volume of water flow**, and the topography creates a significant amount of potential energy.
 
• **Desert areas **are **not suitable **for building large dams as they have low rainfall and a lack of water flow.
 
• **Plains **are** not suitable** for building large dams as the water flow is slow and** does not generate enough potential energy** to generate hydel power.
 
• **Oceans** have a high volume of water flow, but the **water currents are not strong enough** to generate a significant amount of potential energy for generating hydel power.

questions.question: ________ is used to control the demand and supply of money.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Credit control.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Credit control** is used to control the** demand and supply of money.** 
 
• Credit control refers to the actions taken by the **central bank or monetary authority** to regulate the **availability and cost of credit** in the economy.
 
• By controlling the availability of credit, the central bank can influence the demand for money and therefore** control the money supply.**
 
• Credit control is important for maintaining **price stability and preventing inflation.**
 
• If the central bank allows too much credit to be available, it can lead to an **increase in demand for goods and services**, which can cause prices to rise.
 
• By controlling credit, the central bank can** prevent this** from happening.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• One of the main tools used in credit control is the **setting of interest rates.**
 
• By increasing or decreasing interest rates, the central bank can make** credit more or less expensive**, which can influence the demand for money and the money supply.
 
• Other tools used in credit control include **reserve requirements, open market operations, and moral suasion.**
 
• **Reserve requirements** refer to the amount of money that banks are required to** hold in reserve, **which can influence the amount of credit they can lend.
 
• **Open market operations** involve the** buying and selling of government securities**, which can influence the amount of money in circulation.
 
• **Moral suasion **refers to the **use of persuasion and influence** to encourage banks to adopt certain policies or practices.
 
• **Equity control **refers to the **regulation of ownership** in companies and other assets. 
 
• It is not directly related to the **supply and demand of money.**

questions.question: In which layer of the earth do natural earthquakes occur?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lithosphere.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Natural earthquakes** occur in the** lithosphere**, which is the **outermost layer** of the earth.
 
• It includes the crust and the **uppermost part** of the mantle.
 
• The lithosphere is divided into **tectonic plates **that move around on the** asthenosphere**, which is a more fluid layer beneath it.
 
• The movement of these plates creates **stress on the rocks,** which can cause them to break and **release energy **in the form of earthquakes.
 
• The lithosphere is also where most of the **volcanic activity** on earth occurs, as magma rises up from the** mantle** and reaches the surface through cracks in the crust.
 
• The inner core is a solid, dense ball of** iron and nickel **at the center of the earth.
 
• It is **too deep and too hot** for earthquakes to occur there.
 
• The mesosphere is the **layer beneath the lithosphere,** and it is too solid for earthquakes to occur there as well.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **asthenosphere** is a** plastic layer beneath the lithosphere,** where the rocks are partially molten and can flow.

 
 
• It plays a key role in** plate tectonics** and the movement of the** earth's crust.**
 
 
 
• The** inner core** is the **hottest part of the earth**, with temperatures estimated to be as high as **5,500 degrees Celsius**.
 
 
• It is also under **immense pressure,** which keeps it solid despite the high temperatures.
 
 
 
• The **mesosphere** is a relatively **unknown layer of the earth**, as it is difficult to study due to its **depth and lack of seismic activity.**
 
 
• It is thought to be a** transition zone** between the rigid lithosphere and the more fluid asthenosphere.

questions.question: Two successive discounts of 50 percent and 40 percent are equivalent to a single discount of ______.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Two successive discounts of 50% and 40%.

**Concept:**

The formula for successive discounts is D = 100 − [100 − (d₁)] [100 − (d₂)]/100,

where D is the total discount, and d₁ and d₂ are the two given discounts.

**Solution:**

⇒ D = 100 − [100 − (50)][100 − (40)]/100

⇒ D = 100 − [50 × 60]/100

⇒ D = 100 − 30 = 70%

**Therefore, two successive discounts of 50% and 40% are equivalent to a single discount of 70%.**

questions.question: A car travels (1)/(3) of the distance on a straight road at a speed of 10 km/h, the next (1)/(3) at a speed of 20 km/h and the last (1)/(3) at a speed of 60 km/h. Find the average speed of the car.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

1/3 distance at 10 km/h, 1/3 distance at 20 km/h, 1/3 distance at 60 km/h.

**Concept:**

The average speed is total distance divided by total time.

**Solution:**

Time taken in first part of journey = Distance / Speed

⇒ Time1 = (D/3) / 10

Time taken in second part of journey = Distance / Speed

⇒ Time2 = (D/3) / 20

Time taken in last part of journey = Distance / Speed

⇒ Time3 = (D/3) / 60

Total time taken for the entire journey = Sum of time taken in all parts

⇒ Total Time = Time1 + Time2 + Time3

Total Distance covered in the journey = D

Substitute values from steps 1-4 in the formula for average speed:

⇒ Average Speed = D / Total Time

Average Speed = D / [ (D/3)/10 + (D/3)/20 + (D/3)/60 ]

By simplifying above equation,

Average Speed = D / [ (D/30) + (D/60) + (D/180) ]

Average Speed = D / [ (6D + 3D + D) / 180 ]

Average Speed = 180 / 10

**Hence, the average speed of the car is 18 km/h.**

questions.question: Given that 15% of X’s income = 20% of Y’s income = 30% of Z’s income. The sum of their incomes is ₹9,000. If Y spends ₹2,200 from his income, then Y’s saving is:

15% of X = 20% of Y = 30% of Z, X + Y + Z = 9000, Y spends 2200.

**Solution:**

Let 15% of X = 20% of Y = 30% of Z = k.

Then, X = k/0.15, Y = k/0.20, Z = k/0.30.

Substituting in X + Y + Z = 9000, we get k = 600.

Then, Y = k/0.20 = 600/0.20 = 3000.

Y's saving = Y's income - Y's expenditure = 3000 - 2200 = 800.

**Therefore, Y's saving is ₹800.**

questions.question: Find the HCF of 2800 and 756.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Two numbers 2800 and 756.

**Concept:**

The Highest Common Factor (HCF) can be found using the Euclidean Algorithm.

**Solution:**

Apply the Euclidean Algorithm:

⇒ 2800 = 3 × 756 + 532,

⇒ 756 = 1 × 532 + 224,

⇒ 532 = 2 × 224 + 84,

⇒ 224 = 2 × 84 + 56,

⇒ 84 = 1 × 56 + 28,

⇒ 56 = 2 × 28 + 0.

The last non-zero remainder is the HCF.

**Therefore, the HCF of 2800 and 756 is 28.**

questions.question: A heap of sand is in the shape of a right circular cone. It has a slant height of 10 feet and a base diameter of 16 feet. Find the volume of sand making up the heap Take π = 3.14
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a right circular cone, the slant height (l), radius (r), and height (h) form a right-angled triangle.

Given d = 16 ft ⇒ r = 8 ft. Slant height l = 10 ft.

Using Pythagorean triplets (6, 8, 10), the height h = 6 ft.

Volume of a cone = (1÷3) × π × r² × h

V = (1÷3) × 3.14 × 8² × 6 = 2 × 3.14 × 64 = 401.92 ft³

**∴ The correct answer is 401.92 ft³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Slant height of the cone (l) = 10 ft

Base diameter (d) = 16 ft

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/22a7f069662a3d23fc94f2d7e0175d8037b767a4fd9be9de48ce8e75a02c62c5.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a cone = (1÷3) × π × r² × h

Slant height (l) = √(r² + h²)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Radius (r) = d ÷ 2 = 16 ÷ 2 = 8 ft

⇒ Slant height (l) = 10 ft

Applying Pythagoras theorem to find the height (h):

⇒ l² = r² + h²

⇒ 10² = 8² + h²

⇒ 100 = 64 + h²

⇒ h² = 36 ⇒ h = 6 ft

Now, finding the volume of the sand heap:

⇒ Volume = (1÷3) × 3.14 × (8)² × 6

⇒ Volume = 3.14 × 64 × 2

⇒ Volume = 3.14 × 128 = 401.92 ft³

**∴ The correct answer is 401.92 ft³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Curved Surface Area of a Cone

The lateral or curved surface area is given by CSA = π × r × l, where r is the radius and l is the slant height.

Total Surface Area of a Cone

The total surface area includes the base area and is calculated as TSA = π × r × (r + l).

Pythagorean Triplets in Geometry

In cones and right prisms, dimensions often form standard Pythagorean triplets like (3, 4, 5) or (6, 8, 10), which helps in fast mental calculations.

questions.question: A and B can complete a piece of work in 8 days and 16 days respectively. If A and B work on alternate days, starting with B, in how many days the work will be completed?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A can do a job in 8 days, B can do it in 16 days.

**Concept:**

Work done is inversely proportional to the time taken.

**Solution:**

If A's 1 day's work = 1/8, and B's 1 day's work = 1/16.

A and B's 2 day's work = 1/8 + 1/16 = 3/16.

Therefore, the job will be done in (16/3) × 2 = 10.67 days or 11 days approx.

questions.solution:

**Concept:**

Work done is directly proportional to efficiency.

**Solution:**

P's 1 day's work = 3q = 3/60 = 1/20.

**Therefore, P can complete the job alone in 20 days.**

⇒ x = 1360 ÷ 41 ≈ 33.17%

Initial Expenditure = ₹7,200

**Formula Used:**

Savings = Income − Expenditure

Percentage Increase = (Increase in Value ÷ Original Value) × 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Initial Savings = 15400 − 7200 = ₹8,200

⇒ New Income = 15400 + (20% of 15400) = 15400 + 3080 = ₹18,480

Income, Expenditure & Savings Relation

The fundamental equation is Income = Expenditure + Savings. Any percentage change in income is mathematically equivalent to the weighted average of the percentage changes in expenditure and savings.

Alligation Method for Percentage Distribution

When a quantity is split into two parts, the net percentage change of the whole is the mean of the percentage changes of the parts. The ratio of the parts is directly proportional to the difference between their individual changes and the overall average change.

Base Value in Percentages

Always calculate the percentage increase or decrease over the original base value. Percentage change = (Final Value − Initial Value) ÷ Initial Value × 100.

questions.question: A certain number is subtracted from each of the numbers 20, 24, and 29. After the subtraction, the resulting numbers are in proportion. What is the number that was subtracted?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The fastest way to solve this is by testing the options to find a common ratio.

Let's check Option 2, which gives the value 4.

Subtracting 4 from 20, 24, and 29 gives the numbers 16, 20, and 25.

Three numbers are in continued proportion if the ratio of the first to second equals the second to third.

Checking the ratios: 16 ÷ 20 = 4/5 and 20 ÷ 25 = 4/5. The condition is perfectly satisfied.

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Three numbers: 20, 24, and 29

**Formula Used:**

If three numbers a, b, and c are in continued proportion, then a/b = b/c or b² = a × c.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/943d308fa55982c79db6f750341d01f45967d117ac15925974ce4dbcfc97a33b.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the number subtracted from each value be x.

⇒ The new numbers become (20 − x), (24 − x), and (29 − x).

⇒ According to the continued proportion rule: (20 − x) ÷ (24 − x) = (24 − x) ÷ (29 − x)

⇒ Cross-multiplying, we get:

⇒ (20 − x) × (29 − x) = (24 − x)²

⇒ 580 − 20x − 29x + x² = 576 − 48x + x²

⇒ 580 − 49x = 576 − 48x

⇒ 580 − 576 = 49x − 48x

⇒ x = 4

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Proportion

Four numbers a, b, c, and d are said to be in proportion if a ÷ b = c ÷ d, denoted as a:b :: c:d.

Continued Proportion

Three numbers a, b, and c are in continued proportion if a:b = b:c, meaning b² = a × c. Here, b is called the mean proportional between a and c.

Componendo and Dividendo Rule

For any valid proportion a/b = c/d, the rule states that (a + b) ÷ (a − b) = (c + d) ÷ (c − d). This property is highly useful for rapidly simplifying complex fractional equations without cross-multiplying.
</p

Average weight = (4500 + 1800) / (75 + 45) = 52.5 kg.
